newsitem.title: USA: Fund managers get more defensive on US debt-survey.
newsitem.headline: Fund managers get more defensive on US debt-survey.

text.p: Money managers took more-defensive positions in U.S. debt markets last week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Participants shortened up duration exposure over the past week," the report said.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the week ended March 4, duration bogey remained steady at 4.14 on an arithmetic basis and slipped lightly to 4.66 from 4.67 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.84 from 5.16 on an arithmetic basis. It dropped to 4.69 from 4.89 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 7.34 percent from 7.02 percent.
Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 4.0 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active fell to 4.33 from 5.00 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
